title: Anthropic's Quarterly Revenue Jumped 45% to Nearly $17 Billion
summary: Anthropic told public-market investors at a Wednesday meeting that third-quarter revenue rose about 45% to $16.8 billion, ahead of an IPO planned for as soon as next month. Revenue was $11.6 billion in the second quarter and just under $5 billion in the first, though The Information notes growth is slowing from the Q2 pace of more than 140%, which could force the company to keep its valuation target in check.

title: Tech Stocks Slide Again as CoreWeave Extends Plunge
summary: Tech shares were headed for another rough session as AI jitters combined with rate-hike fears, with CoreWeave falling further premarket after a 15% drop the prior day and South Korea's Kospi and Japan's Nikkei dropping about 7% and 5%. The Information adds that heavily indebted neocloud CoreWeave has issued $4.2 billion of convertible notes and may sell up to 35 million shares, while its CEO has sold stock every week since April.

title: Bloomberg CEO's 'Aggressive' Stance on AI
summary: Bloomberg has made its conversational AI interface, ASKB, available to all Terminal users, and the latest version lets clients combine their own content such as watchlists and chats with Bloomberg data. CEO Vlad Kliatchko says it is premature to focus on AI ROI and that the privately held company is investing aggressively out of strategic conviction, a stance the column contrasts with public-market sentiment.

title: AI Companies Play Cat and Mouse With Secret-Stealing Spies
summary: Leading AI labs are increasingly worried about insider risk as rapid hiring and frequent moves between rivals make leaks harder to prevent. The report cites OpenAI's court claim that a former employee who went to Apple sent himself more than 100 confidential files, and the charging of a Saudi OpenAI employee accused of planting a recording device in a conference room.

title: AI Demand Extends TSMC's Record Earnings Streak
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing's third-quarter net profit jumped a better-than-expected 69% to $23.71 billion, and it guided fourth-quarter revenue of $52.3 billion to $54.3 billion on continued AI chip demand. CEO C.C. Wei said TSMC has sent teams to Texas to assess further US expansion and confirmed talks about Elon Musk's Terafab project.

title: Proofpoint to Acquire Varonis in $6.3 Billion Cybersecurity Deal
summary: Proofpoint has agreed to acquire data-security company Varonis Systems for about $6.3 billion. The deal underscores how AI-related security concerns continue to drive M&A and investment across the cybersecurity industry.

title: Meta and Apple, Longtime Foes, Team Up to Put Open-Weight AI on Macs
summary: Meta and Apple are partnering to bring open-weight AI models to Macs, giving developers a way to run sophisticated models locally instead of renting cloud computing power. The tie-up is notable given the companies' long rivalry.

title: OpenAI's Accelerates Ad Sprint With Meta Hires, Slashed Prices
summary: OpenAI is speeding up its advertising business, hiring dozens of people from Meta and cutting prices to attract advertisers. The report points to a deliberate push to build out ads as a revenue line.

title: Cursor Staff Investigated Whether Confidential Data Reached SpaceX for AI Training
summary: Cursor employees looked into whether confidential data about the coding startup's customers and business partners ended up at SpaceX and was used for AI training. The exclusive raises data-governance questions around Cursor's ties to SpaceX.

title: Cognition's Plan to Limit Tokenmaxxing to the Most Efficient Engineers
summary: AI coding startup Cognition is rolling out a feature that lets companies manage AI spending by tracking how efficiently their engineers use tokens. The approach would restrict heavy token consumption to the most efficient engineers.

title: Is the Next Hot AI Startup a Flight Simulator for Software?
summary: As AI-written applications multiply, companies say demand is rising for deterministic simulators that repeatedly stress-test software against network failures and attacks. Antithesis, used by Replit, Palantir and Datadog, says it added more revenue in the August quarter than in the five prior quarters combined; it raised $105 million at a $525 million valuation in late 2025 and may raise again soon.

title: Jio Targets Up to $3.2B in Imminent IPO
summary: Jio Platforms has set the price band for its IPO, with the company set to raise a maximum of INR302.1 billion, or about $3.2 billion, from the share sale.

title: GlobalFoundries to Run Japan-Funded US Chip Sites
summary: Japan will provide $20 billion in funding for two new semiconductor facilities in the US under a bilateral trade agreement, with GlobalFoundries selected to operate the sites.

title: Ericsson Q3 Fuelled by Strong Networks Sales
summary: Ericsson reported a healthy rise in third-quarter 2026 revenue, helped by higher sales in its Networks division. New CEO Per Narvinger cautioned about potential headwinds over the next year.

title: Cohere Plans to Acquire Cyber Startup Aisle and Set Up New Security Division
summary: Canadian AI company Cohere plans to acquire cybersecurity startup Aisle and create a new security division. The deal would add security tools for customers wanting more control over their AI systems and expand Cohere's business in Europe.

title: Canadian Entrepreneurs Are Chasing Growth Again, Despite Trade Uncertainty
summary: A new BDC survey finds Canadian businesses are expanding their customers, markets and suppliers while stepping up efforts to boost productivity, despite ongoing trade uncertainty.

title: Coinbase Wants to Put Bots on the Blockchain
summary: A Coinbase-backed lobby group argues in a new report that Canada could lead the growing market for AI agent-led crypto transactions.

title: AI Runs Into Its Next Big Obstacle: Insurance
summary: Safety incidents and lawsuits are exposing the largest AI developers to potential liabilities running into the tens or even hundreds of billions of dollars, yet specialized AI insurance is scarce. Munich Re's policy tops out at $50 million, and some industry officials want the US government to provide a liability backstop. A major incident causing widespread harm could overwhelm an AI company's financial buffers, and businesses that use the technology are exposed too.

title: AI Hyperscalers Try to Fix Their 'Storytelling Problem'
summary: Facing hundreds of proposed moratoriums and dozens of scrapped projects, Google and Amazon are disclosing data-center plans earlier and offering community investment to win over skeptical locals. Amazon says it will no longer use NDAs with local officials, while Google has launched a 'We're listening' site and survey for New Mexico's Lea County. Opponents say the moves show tech companies have lost control of the narrative, with water use emerging as a top community concern.

title: AI Agents Bring New Headaches to Online Sellers
summary: AI shopping agents such as Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots are helping millions of people decide on purchases and bid in online auctions, inserting themselves between businesses and customers. For many e-commerce companies this is as much a problem as an opportunity, because firms skilled at winning search and social traffic have no clear playbook for agent-driven traffic.

title: Nvidia, Meta and Apple Unveil New Open Models
summary: Nvidia released three new open models in its Nemotron family aimed at helping companies build AI agents, including Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, which handles images and video as well as text. Atlassian, CrowdStrike, Dassault Systemes, Salesforce and Synopsys have customized the model with their own data. Nvidia says interest is rising because the models are US-made with inspectable training data, though it is too soon to tell whether they will pull developers away from cheaper Chinese open models.

title: AI Boom-or-Bust Scenarios Loom Large at World Financial Summit
summary: The economic possibilities and potential perils of AI dominated discussions at the IMF gathering in Bangkok this week. Policymakers and financial leaders weighed scenarios in which the AI investment boom either lifts growth or turns into a bust.

title: Netflix Replaces Content Chief as It Struggles to Engage Viewers
summary: Netflix Chief Content Officer Bela Bajaria is leaving as the company contends with slowing growth and falling customer engagement. She will be succeeded by Peter Rice, a former 21st Century Fox and Disney executive.

title: 'Cyber Incident' Halts Key US Bankruptcy Notice Services
summary: The federal organization that produces and transmits notices for all US bankruptcy courts says operations are down after contractor BAE Systems was hit in a cyber incident. Sites supporting the Bankruptcy Noticing Center, including the National Creditor Registration Service, are unavailable, and court notices indicate the outage affecting paper and electronic transmissions has lasted since Oct. 9.

title: CenterPoint Energy Data Breach Impacts 1 Million Texans
summary: CenterPoint Energy disclosed that more than one million Texas residents had personal data stolen in a September cyberattack, including Social Security and driver's license numbers. The Houston-based utility did not say whether customers in Indiana, Minnesota and Ohio were affected. It had told the SEC in September that it was investigating hackers' online claims of stealing customer information.

title: Apple's Antitrust Settlement Talks Spur Worries Among Developers
summary: Apple's settlement talks with the US Justice Department over its antitrust case are raising concerns among developers such as Epic Games and PayPal, according to The Information. Early settlement discussions between Apple and the DOJ were first reported in July.

title: Singapore's DayOne Pushes Ahead With Data Center IPO Tied to TikTok
summary: Singapore-based data center operator DayOne is moving forward with an IPO tied to TikTok, according to The Information. The company has previously been reported to be weighing a listing in the US, possibly alongside Singapore.

title: Smartphone Shipments Tank to Record Quarterly Low
summary: Global smartphone shipments fell 22% in the third quarter of 2026, the steepest decline on record, according to IDC. The drop is attributed to the ongoing AI-driven memory crisis.

title: Reliance Snaps Back at Musk Over Ambani Claims
summary: Reliance Industries appeared to respond to Elon Musk's suggestion that Mukesh Ambani is blocking Starlink's entry into India, saying it welcomes competition. Reliance also pointed out that its own satellite venture has not yet been cleared by regulators.

title: Verizon, Ericsson Claim First 7GHz 6G Field Call
summary: Verizon and Ericsson say they completed the first pre-standard 6G field call in the 7GHz range, moving testing from the laboratory to a commercial network site.

title: Flaws in CPP Legislation Have Left Billions at Stake Ahead of Alberta's Referendum
summary: Flaws in the legislation governing the Canada Pension Plan have left billions of dollars at stake ahead of Alberta's referendum on leaving the plan, according to The Logic. Pension experts say an Alberta exit could drive up contribution rates for workers and employers in other provinces.

title: Anthropic's Late IPO
summary: The Information's Martin Peers argues Anthropic may have waited too long to go public, as third-quarter figures implied growth slowed from the second quarter and investors see an IPO valuation nearer $1.4 to $1.5 trillion than the $2 trillion bankers floated. He cites competition from cheaper open models and more than $500 billion in compute commitments as added risks to owning the stock.

title: Apple's Value Amid Frontier AI Spending
summary: Apple shares are up 26% this year, versus 10% to 12% for Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Microsoft, and Apple is the only one of the group whose valuation multiple has risen, according to Koyfin data. The column argues that growing doubts about the value of frontier AI models suggest Apple was right to avoid the costly race to build its own.

title: Anthropic revealed as client for EverWind's $10B Nova Scotia data centre
summary: The Logic reports that Anthropic is the customer behind EverWind's roughly $10 billion data centre project in Nova Scotia. The 95-megawatt facility is intended to power Anthropic's Claude AI models and is slated to come online in late 2027.

title: AI Agents Trading Stocks While You Sleep? Charles Schwab's CEO Is Skeptical
summary: Charles Schwab CEO Rick Wurster is skeptical that autonomous AI agents will take over investing on behalf of retail clients. He is betting that money and investing needs still call for a human touch, a stance that contrasts with the industry push toward agent-driven trading.

title: Meta Reports Early as Heavy AI Spending Puts Cash Flow in Focus
summary: Meta reports September-quarter earnings on Wednesday, a week before Google, Microsoft and Amazon, with first-half ad revenue up 30% but analysts expecting capex of $40.5 billion, double the prior year. That is projected to produce negative free cash flow of about $10.3 billion, the first of several such quarters, and Meta's $90 billion cash pile may eventually need topping up with debt or equity.

title: China Weighs New Export Controls on AI Models and Chip Designs
summary: China's Ministry of Commerce issued a draft plan adding 40 technologies across AI, biomedicine and photovoltaics to its list of restricted technologies. The measure could limit overseas transfers of AI models and chip designs deemed strategically important.

title: Microsoft Pulls Out of Nscale U.K. Data Center Over Power Delays
summary: Microsoft withdrew from a planned U.K. data center that Nscale was building for it after the site faced delays securing power. The cancellation could weigh on Nscale's planned public offering this month as investors question whether AI cloud providers can generate revenue fast enough to service their debts.

title: Anthropic Creates Public Benefit Fund With at Least 5% of Its Shares
summary: Anthropic announced a new fund committed to receiving at least 5% of its shares, to support causes such as addressing AI's employment impact. The fund could receive an additional 2% at the board's discretion for every 50% increase in Anthropic's valuation.

title: Nvidia-Backed Startup doubleAI Launches Model to Pare Cost of Compute
summary: DoubleAI, co-founded by Mobileye's Amnon Shashua, is launching what it calls a new category of AI, 'code execution models,' that run inside live programs to use existing hardware more efficiently. The company says it cut one early customer's compute costs by 67% and has raised $220 million from investors including Lightspeed, Bessemer, Nvidia and Dell.

title: Jamie Dimon Tells Leaders to Ramp Up Cyber Defenses
summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon said cybersecurity is now the bank's biggest risk 'by far' following the arrival of powerful AI models such as Anthropic's Mythos-based systems. He urged companies to start immediately on network segmentation, identity and access management, and AI-driven vulnerability scanning, and flagged critical infrastructure and vendor supply chains as particular weak points.

title: The Weak Points in AI Bonds Are Becoming Clearer
summary: Traders are identifying where they see the biggest pitfalls in debt issuance tied to artificial intelligence, as investor pressure mounts on heavily indebted AI infrastructure firms. The column highlights growing scrutiny of the credit structures financing the AI build-out.

title: Temu Pays $3 Million to Settle Data Privacy Case in Texas
summary: Temu agreed to pay $3 million to resolve Texas allegations that it shared residents' data with the Chinese government, without admitting wrongdoing. The settlement requires Texans' data to be stored on U.S. servers and the shopping apps to undergo annual third-party security testing, and similar suits in Missouri, Arizona and other states remain pending.

title: Cybersecurity Stocks Fall 16.4% in a Week as AI Cyber Fears Mount
summary: The WSJ Pro CyberIndex fell 16.4% for the week, with Okta down more than 20% and Cloudflare, Palo Alto Networks and SentinelOne each losing more than 17%; only Leidos finished higher. Separately, the G-7 agreed to run joint exercises to prepare for AI-powered cyberattacks, possibly including global banks.

title: Former OpenAI Worker Accused of Bugging Discussed Jobs With Saudi Royal
summary: In a detention filing, prosecutors argue that Abdulrahman Alfozan, a former OpenAI worker accused of bugging, is a flight risk because his wife and child have moved permanently to Saudi Arabia. The filing says he discussed jobs with a Saudi royal.

title: U.A.E.-Based AI and Data Startup Expands Into Silicon Valley
summary: CNTXT AI, which raised $60 million in June, is opening a Silicon Valley presence. The startup has built Arabic-first AI models and is training robots.

title: What to Know About the Obscure Private Trust Looming Over Anthropic's IPO
summary: Ahead of its IPO, Anthropic has shared few details about the dynamics of a five-person trust that is empowered to shape its board and block major moves. The structure raises governance questions for prospective public investors.

title: Quantinuum Reports Error-Correction Milestone, Targets Fault-Tolerant Quantum by 2029
summary: Quantinuum said it reached a technical milestone addressing qubits' tendency to produce errors from tiny environmental disturbances. The company says this puts it on a path to fully accurate, reliable quantum computers by 2029.

title: How DeepSeek Is Shaping Huawei's AI Chips in a Growing Challenge to Nvidia
summary: The Information reports that China's DeepSeek is quietly influencing the design of Huawei's AI chips, in what it describes as a growing challenge to Nvidia. The piece, by Qianer Liu and Juro Osawa, points to deepening ties between Chinese AI labs and domestic chipmakers.

title: Anthropic Readies Model That Reads Users' Intentions Better
summary: The Information reports that Anthropic is preparing to release a model that shows better intuition about what users intend. The article is by Stephanie Palazzolo.

title: Pentagon's Emil Michael Vows Export Controls if AI Labs Don't Cooperate With Government
summary: In an interview with The Information, Pentagon official Emil Michael vowed to use export controls on AI labs that do not cooperate with the government. The remarks signal a harder line on how U.S. national security agencies intend to deal with frontier AI developers.

title: How Microsoft's New Office Chief Fixed Copilot and Won Over Nadella
summary: Charles Lamanna convinced Satya Nadella in 2025 to pay for Anthropic's models to fix a buggy Copilot, a pitch he called 'heresy' at the time. Copilot's corporate users have since more than doubled to over 30 million, and Lamanna's organization has grown to roughly 25,000 people spanning Copilot, Office and Teams, with some senior executives viewing him as a potential Nadella successor.

title: European Operators Confirm Satellite Spectrum Move
summary: Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Telefonica and Vodafone signed a letter of intent to explore a joint bid for future Mobile Satellite Services spectrum. The move is part of efforts to advance direct-to-device connectivity in Europe.

title: Report Finds Telco Jobs Fall as Labour Costs Rise
summary: Global telecom employment fell 2.1% year on year in the second quarter of 2026, according to MTN Consulting, extending a decline that dates back to 2016. The report notes labour costs are rising even as headcount shrinks.

title: Apple iPhone Duo Delivery Dates Slip Into 2027
summary: Apple's first foldable smartphone hit a supply crunch within minutes of preorders opening, with delivery estimates for the iPhone Duo slipping into January 2027.

title: Starlink Connectivity Revenue Up 66% to $4.3 Billion, GSMA Satellite Tracker Finds
summary: GSMA Intelligence's Q3 2026 satellite and non-terrestrial networks tracker cites SpaceX's Q2 results showing Starlink connectivity revenue up 66% year on year to $4.3 billion. It says spectrum access, regulatory alignment and operator integration are becoming more important in the competitive landscape.
